title: Act 1 repo: payments-ledger with planted defect, planted violation and fallback patch
story: As the candidate I need a realistic small Python payments service with a one-cent fee bug and a PAN-logging violation, plus a verified reference fix, so that Act 1 shows onboarding, test-first bug fixing and governance to the 120 software engineers' stack without depending on luck.
acceptance: Given the repo, when `wc -l demo/payments-ledger/ledger/*.py` runs, then ledger/ holds __init__.py, models.py, fees.py, fx.py, settlement.py and refunds.py totalling 400-700 lines, with type hints on public functions and module docstrings; only stdlib is imported (pytest only in tests/).

Given the start state, when `cd demo/payments-ledger && python3 -m pytest -q` runs, then it exits non-zero and the ONLY failures are the parametrized cases in tests/test_fee_rounding_pay1423.py (at least 3 failing cases); every other test passes (at least 20 other tests); counts are recorded in demo/fallback/act1/README.md.

Given tickets/PAY-1423.md, then it is a merchant complaint (fictional merchant, synthetic-data footer) quoting at least 4 concrete transaction amounts with statement fee vs merchant-expected fee, and the contractual rule (half-up to the cent); a short Python snippet using Decimal ROUND_HALF_UP reproduces the expected values and the float round() path reproduces the statement values.

Given the code, then fees.py is the only module that converts money to float or uses round() on money; fx.py, settlement.py and refunds.py use Decimal and quantize half-up to cents (fx.py is the intended pattern for Claude to copy).

Given settlement.py, then exactly one logging call passes payment.card_number (the line logger.debug("settling payment %s card=%s amount=%s", payment.id, payment.card_number, payment.amount)); no 13-19 digit PAN literal exists in ledger/; Luhn-valid test PANs appear only in tests/fixtures/; tests/test_no_pan_literals.py scans the repo outside tests/fixtures/ and passes.

Given CLAUDE.md, then it states: money is Decimal quantized half-up to cents; never log PANs, log last4 tokens (card_last4); run pytest before claiming done; plus how to run tests and a glossary of at least 8 payments terms (PAN, last4, processing fee, settlement batch, minor units, chargeback, refund, idempotency key). Rules are written as team policy; it asserts no PCI DSS requirement text. README.md explains the service, layout, and the one-line test command.

Given demo/fallback/act1/PAY-1423.patch (paths relative to the payments-ledger root, `patch -p1`), when applied to a `cp -r` copy in the scratchpad, then it applies cleanly and `python3 -m pytest -q` is fully green, including added regression tests (half-cent boundaries, refund fee consistency, a Decimal-oracle sweep over a range of cent amounts); PAN-LOG-fix.patch (switches the log line to card_last4 and adds a caplog test) applies alone and together with the first patch, all green.

Given demo/fallback/act1/README.md, then it records the exact commands run, date, Python version, and pass/fail counts for: start state, PAY-1423.patch applied, PAN-LOG-fix.patch applied, both applied.

Given the folder tree, then demo/payments-ledger/.claude/ and demo/payments-ledger/.env do not exist from this ticket, no `claude` CLI was run, and no Python syntax newer than 3.10 is used (no tomllib, typing.Self, except*, datetime.UTC).
node org/contracts/validate.mjs passes (it scans demo/ for [CLM-###] citations); any placeholder is written [CLM-?: ...].
brief:
Build the Act 1 repo for the live demo (5 minutes on stage: tour an unfamiliar payments service, fix a one-cent fee bug test-first, flag a PAN-logging violation). The CTO has read real payments code, so it must look like a team's code, not a toy. Python 3.10+, stdlib + pytest, money as Decimal.

Structure: ledger/{__init__,models,fees,fx,settlement,refunds}.py with module loggers and docstrings; tests/ with unit tests per module and tests/fixtures/cards.json (synthetic Luhn-valid test PANs from public test ranges); tickets/PAY-1423.md; CLAUDE.md; README.md; pyproject.toml (pytest testpaths = tests); .gitignore. Domain: Payment(id, merchant_id, amount, currency, card_number, created) with property card_last4; per-merchant fee schedule (percent + fixed cents, e.g. 2.9% + 30c); fx.py converts with Decimal and quantizes half-up (the intended pattern); settlement.py groups payments into per-merchant batches and renders merchant statements with per-payment fees and totals; refunds.py reverses fees pro rata via fees.py.

Defect PAY-1423: fees.py goes through float and round(). Brute-force cent amounts to find ones where the float path differs from Decimal ROUND_HALF_UP; pick 4+ and use the same numbers in the ticket and the test. Everything else stays correct so pytest fails only in tests/test_fee_rounding_pay1423.py (its own file so the Sprint 2 setup script can add or remove it for a test-first prompt).

Violation: exactly one line in settlement.py, the logger.debug line quoted in the acceptance criteria. Interface agreed with S1-DEM-03 (governance, runs in parallel): field names card_number (full PAN, in-memory only) and card_last4; full PAN literals live only under tests/fixtures/ because its PCI hook allows exactly that path; its tests use your exact debug line.

CLAUDE.md: team rules as policy, never as claims about what PCI DSS requires (if you must, write [CLM-?: ...]). Merchant names, ids and amounts are fictional; end tickets with a synthetic-data note.

Fallback: write the two patches and verify on a cp -r copy in the scratchpad, then record the runs. .gitignore ignores only caches and virtualenvs (S1-DEM-03 ships a committed fake .env and .claude/). Never create .claude/ or .env here and never run the claude CLI.
